title: Wildfire-smoke deaths are upside-down — the toll is in the global South

bars.label: Rest of the low- & middle-income world

provenance.definition: Landscape-fire smoke is attributed ~1.53 million deaths a year; more than 90% fall in low- and middle-income countries and ~39% in sub-Saharan Africa — savanna and crop burning, not the televised megafires. Smoke out-kills flame roughly 10:1 (Australia’s 2019–20 Black Summer: 417 smoke deaths vs 33 from flame).
provenance.attribution: Chen et al. 2024 (The Lancet Planetary Health)

recipe.detail: Where landscape-fire smoke deaths actually fall, by income geography.
